cards.title: Schedule Agreement
cards.content: Set a fixed weekly time (e.g., 90 min) and a start time.

cards.title: Create Disturbance-Free Space
cards.content: Ensure a quiet environment without distractions or visitors.

cards.title: Establish Clear Rules
cards.content: Agree on a fixed speaking time (e.g., 15 min) and strict listening protocol.

cards.title: Ritual Foundation
cards.content: Make the session a fixed, non-negotiable ritual that isn't skipped.

cards.title: Radical Empathy
cards.content: Your only task is to listen with full attention, without your own agenda.

cards.title: Strict Taboos
cards.content: Absolute prohibition: No interrupting, judging, advising, or non-verbal rejection (e.g., eye-rolling).

cards.title: Embrace Silence
cards.content: When your partner pauses to think, remain still even if the silence feels long.

cards.title: Speaker/Listener Roles
cards.content: The speaker says 'I think/feel...', the listener only listens attentively without judgment.

cards.title: Call Time-Out
cards.content: Stop the conversation as soon as you or your partner feel emotionally overwhelmed.

cards.title: Calm Down Physically
cards.content: Use the pause for calming activities (e.g., reading, walking), not to brood.

cards.title: Resume Conversation
cards.content: Resume the dialogue within 24 hours to avoid the conflict from escalating.

beforeSession.title: Before the Session
beforeSession.item1: Schedule a fixed weekly time (e.g., 90 min) and set a specific start time
beforeSession.item2: Create a quiet, disturbance-free environment without distractions
beforeSession.item3: Agree on a fixed speaking time (e.g., 15 min) and strict listening protocol
beforeSession.item4: Make the session a fixed, non-negotiable ritual

duringSession.title: During the Session
duringSession.item1: Your only task as listener is to listen with full attention, without your own agenda
duringSession.item2: Absolute prohibition: No interrupting, judging, advising, or non-verbal rejection
duringSession.item3: When your partner pauses to think, remain still even if the silence feels long
duringSession.item4: As speaker, use "I feel/think" expressions and avoid accusations

whenTriggered.title: When I Feel Triggered
whenTriggered.item1: Call time-out as soon as you or your partner feel emotionally overwhelmed
whenTriggered.item2: Use the pause for calming activities, not to brood
whenTriggered.item3: Resume the dialogue within 24 hours to prevent escalation
whenTriggered.item4: Focus on understanding rather than defending

intro.title: Welcome to Couples Timer
intro.subtitle: Your guide to structured partner conversations
intro.description: This tool helps you practice the Zwiegespräch method - a structured conversation technique that creates space for deep connection and understanding between partners.

moeller.title: The Zwiegespräch Method
moeller.description: Developed by psychologist Michael Lukas Moeller, the Zwiegespräch is a structured dialogue method that has helped thousands of couples deepen their connection through regular, intentional conversations.

principle1.title: Equal speaking time
principle1.desc: Each partner gets the same amount of uninterrupted time to express themselves.

principle2.title: No interruptions
principle2.desc: The listening partner remains silent, giving full attention without responding.

principle3.title: Active listening
principle3.desc: Focus entirely on understanding, not on formulating your response.

adaptations.title: Our Adaptations
adaptations.description: We've enhanced the classic method with features designed to deepen the experience and support emotional connection.

transition.title: 1-minute silent transition
transition.desc: After each speaking turn, a moment of silence helps process what was shared and prepare for what comes next.

regulation.title: Emotional regulation
regulation.desc: The pause prevents reactive responses and gives space for emotions to settle naturally.

audio.title: Gentle singing bowl cues
audio.desc: Subtle audio signals mark phase transitions, so you can stay present without watching the clock.

maintain.title: Maintain Mode
maintain.desc: Weekly relationship maintenance conversation - keep connection strong

commitment.title: Commitment Mode
commitment.desc: Stabilization during crisis phases - more frequent, focused sessions

listening.title: Listening Mode
listening.desc: Beginner-friendly mode with more guidance - perfect for starting out

custom.title: Custom Mode
custom.description: For advanced users who want full control over their conversation structure. Once you're familiar with the method, create your own perfect session.

feature1.title: Adjust phase durations
feature1.desc: Set exactly how long each speaking turn and transition lasts.

feature2.title: Choose number of rounds
feature2.desc: Add or remove rounds to match your available time.

feature3.title: Save your configuration
feature3.desc: Create and save multiple custom modes for different situations.

custom.tip: Tip: Start with a preset mode to learn the rhythm before customizing.

ready.title: Choose Your Mode
ready.subtitle: We recommend starting with Listening Mode for your first conversation.
ready.note: Select a mode, then click "Start Session" to begin your first conversation.

r1.1: What did you enjoy about me this week – a small moment you like to remember?
r1.2: Is there something I did this week that deserves a bit of praise? Tell me about it.
r1.3: Which day of this week was your favorite – and what made it special?

r2.1: How does appreciation reach you most clearly – through words, gestures, time, or something else?
r2.2: Was there a moment this week when you wished for more recognition?
r2.3: Where is it easy for you to show me gratitude, and where is it harder?

r3.1: Is there something about you that you wish I would notice and value more often?
r3.2: When does appreciation from me feel less than genuine – and what would need to change?
r3.3: Which part of you feels especially precious to you that I rarely mention?

r1.1: When did you feel seen or understood by me this week?
r1.2: Which compliment from this week has stayed with you – from anyone at all?
r1.3: What would you like to say out loud right now about what you love about us?

r2.1: Honestly: how well did I show this week that I cherish you?
r2.2: What sometimes keeps you from telling me what you like about me in everyday life?
r2.3: If we introduced a small ritual of gratitude – what would it look like?

r3.1: When was it last hard for you to accept a thank-you from me – and how did that feel?
r3.2: Were there times in our relationship when you felt less appreciated? What has changed since?
r3.3: How would you like to be appreciated by me exactly as you are – not as you should be?

r1.1: What was your biggest everyday strain this week – and how did you handle it?
r1.2: Which small chore or duty is annoying you the most right now?
r1.3: Was there a moment when you thought: “I could use a hand right now”?

r2.1: How did we make everyday life easier for each other this week – or harder?
r2.2: Does the way our tasks are divided feel right to you?
r2.3: What would ease this week for you the most, even if it is something small?

r3.1: Is there a load you have carried for a long time that we have never really talked about?
r3.2: What makes it hard for you to ask for relief before it becomes too much?
r3.3: If we could put down one of your burdens for good – which one would it be?

r1.1: What did everyday life throw at you this week without any warning?
r1.2: Where did you feel this week that you were carrying something alone?
r1.3: Which daily routine helps you best get through the week?

r2.1: Where do we notice too little what the other one is carrying?
r2.2: How does the pace of the last few weeks feel to you – too fast, too slow, about right?
r2.3: Which burden do you quietly carry because you believe it is only yours?

r3.1: When did you last feel completely exhausted and hide it anyway?
r3.2: Which everyday worry weighs on you, even if it may be unlikely?
r3.3: What would it take for you to confide in me when everything feels like too much?

r1.1: What did you wish for this week that you did not get – no matter how small?
r1.2: If you had a free day tomorrow: would you spend it alone or with me – and how?
r1.3: What would you still like to experience together with me this week?

r2.1: Which longing has accompanied you for a while – in our life together or within yourself?
r2.2: How have your wishes for us changed since we have been together?
r2.3: How do you recognize that a wish of yours truly matters?

r3.1: What do you wish for from us – or from yourself – so deeply that you almost never say it?
r3.2: Is there a dream you gave up on? Would you like to talk about it?
r3.3: If anything were possible: what would a day look like after which you would say you received everything you need?

r1.1: Which wish is very present for you right now, even if it seems out of reach?
r1.2: Is there something you are secretly looking forward to – and what is it?
r1.3: If you could pick one thing for our tomorrow – what would it be?

r2.1: Which of your wishes has gotten too little room in our everyday life so far?
r2.2: How would you like to feel about us in five years – and what would that take?
r2.3: Is there a wish you prefer to keep to yourself? Would you like to share it anyway?

r3.1: What do you fear when you think about speaking your deeper wishes out loud?
r3.2: Which of your longings is about our relationship – and which is not?
r3.3: What would you like to be allowed in our relationship, even though you have not dared it so far?

r1.1: Was there a moment this week when we talked past each other – and how did we find our way back to each other?
r1.2: How do you notice in yourself that a misunderstanding needs clearing up?
r1.3: What helps you fastest when something feels tense between us?

r2.1: What does reconciliation look like between us – and which role do I play in it, which one do you?
r2.2: Is there something you have recently wanted to apologize to me for?
r2.3: What do you do when you sense that I am not ready to clear things up yet?

r3.1: Is there something older between us that you have forgiven – or would still like to forgive?
r3.2: What does reconciliation do to you – and what does it need from me to feel real?
r3.3: Which old argument would you like to have differently, if it were possible?

r1.1: Is there something small from this week still standing between us that you would like to bring up?
r1.2: How do I show you – perhaps unintentionally – that something is still unresolved?
r1.3: What does us the most good after an argument?

r2.1: How do you feel when I apologize to you – is it easy for you to accept?
r2.2: What does an apology from me need so that it truly reaches you?
r2.3: Is there a topic where we keep sliding into the same conflict?

r3.1: Is there something where you feel you have not fully let go, even though it seemed settled?
r3.2: What makes forgiving hardest for you – and what might help?
r3.3: Being completely honest: what do you need from me to feel safe with us again?

r1.1: Which shared plan are you looking forward to next – and what exactly about it?
r1.2: What have we talked about lately that you would like to take on?
r1.3: What would be a lovely next step for the two of us?

r2.1: What belongs to a good shared life for you – beyond plans and appointments?
r2.2: How do we handle wishes where we do not see eye to eye?
r2.3: Which part of our future do we shape deliberately – and where are we drifting?

r3.1: Which question about our shared future occupies you the most right now – and do you let it in?
r3.2: What would you like to be able to say about our life today in ten years?
r3.3: Is there something you fear about our future? Would you like to say it here?

r1.1: Where do you see us in a year – in broad strokes?
r1.2: Is there something you are quietly already preparing for our future?
r1.3: What would you like to be able to look back on a year from now and say?

r2.1: Which shared goal gives you strength right now – and which one rather drains you?
r2.2: How important are reliability and planning to you – and how much surprise does your life need?
r2.3: What would you like to do consciously differently in our future than in your past?

r3.1: When you think of growing old together: how would you like us to treat each other then?
r3.2: Which values should guide our decisions – and where do we already live them today?
r3.3: What does our relationship need so that it keeps growing over many years?

r1.1: How much space for yourself did you have this week – enough, too little, just right?
r1.2: Is there something you did not say this week because you were being considerate?
r1.3: What is your favorite moment to yourself – and how often does it fit into your day?

r2.1: Where might our boundaries have quietly blurred lately – to both of our disadvantage?
r2.2: What makes it hard for you to put your boundaries into words with me?
r2.3: How do I notice that you feel a boundary has been crossed – and how would you like to show me?

r3.1: Is there a boundary you have not voiced for a long time because you wanted to keep the peace?
r3.2: What do you fear when you think of saying “no” more clearly in our relationship?
r3.3: How may I support you when you feel squeezed between me and yourself?

r1.1: When did you set a boundary well lately – and when hardly at all?
r1.2: What do you need to feel safe enough with me to say “no”?
r1.3: How do you feel when I need time just for myself?

r2.1: Which boundary of yours would you like to live more clearly – and what holds you back?
r2.2: How can we give each other more room without either of us feeling left behind?
r2.3: Were there moments when you felt my boundaries – how did you handle them?

r3.1: Were there times in your life when your boundaries mattered little? What did that do to you?
r3.2: What would a togetherness look like in which both of us remain fully ourselves?
r3.3: If you could voice one boundary right now without anything shifting – which one would it be?
